There is a real difference. structuredClone keeps Date, Map, Set, typed arrays, undefined values and circular references, and throws on functions or DOM nodes; the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, turns Map/Set into empty objects, drops undefined and functions, and throws on circular references. Prefer structuredClone unless you specifically want a JSON-safe copy. Action: none needed; I can grep the PR's usages if you want to see which ones would actually behave differently.

They're different. Keep-alive just reuses one TCP connection for several requests, but on HTTP/1.1 they still go one at a time per connection (so browsers open several connections), and a slow response blocks the ones behind it. HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent request/response streams over a single connection, with binary framing and header compression. Action: none needed; I can check which protocol our servers actually negotiate if you want it for the standup thread.

`as const` changes the inferred type (literals stay literal, everything readonly) and checks nothing; `satisfies` checks the value against a type without changing its inferred type. A Deployment treats pods as interchangeable and stateless: any pod can be replaced or scaled freely. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable identity (ordered names like name-0, stable network ID) and its own persistent volume that follows it across reschedules, with ordered rollout. Pick it for databases and brokers where each replica needs its own storage or a stable address. Action: none needed.
